question_type: sum of one country's monthly capital-movements liabilities across three years (revised vintage), converted to GBP at a date-pinned, pre-rounded exchange rate

opus_path.decision: Series = CM 'Total Liabilities by Country', UK row, end-of-June positions; sum three Junes in $M; convert with a 'USD to GBP' rate read as GBP per 1 USD, rounded to hundredths BEFORE converting; listed the ambiguities up front (two tables with the same title, preliminary vs revised, rate direction, June 30 2002 was a Sunday).
Chose CM-I (bank-reported, monthly) over CM-IV-2 (nonbank, quarterly, much smaller) because the question stresses calendar months.
Mapped every printing: June of year Y is printed only as 'June p' in the Sept-Y issue and revised in the Dec-Y issue; no later reprint. Took the Dec issues (latest revision, no issue pinned).
Read each Dec-issue header and took the cell under the 'June' header; checked alignment by comparing the calendar-year and 'May' columns with the Sept printing.
Exchange rate from the FCP Sterling Positions monthly/quarterly June 2002 row (USD per pound), not the 06/26 weekly row; inverted to GBP per USD, then rounded to hundredths.
calc.py reads the cited cells by line/column with asserts on the row label and computes the chosen route plus the three alternatives (prelim/latest x multiply/divide).
Magnitude and revision-size sanity checks; the reviewer flagged the answer 'Uncertain' because of vintage and rate-source ambiguity, but found no error.

opus_key_moves: Enumerated every printing of each June cell and took the December (revised) issue
Selected each cell by its column header and cross-checked alignment against the neighbouring 'May' and calendar-year columns of the other printing
Resolved the rate direction explicitly (USD to GBP = GBP per USD, rounded before converting) and printed all alternative routes

first_divergence.what_glm_did: Took all three Junes from the September issues (the 'June p' preliminary column). It saw that the Dec 2002 issue revised June 2002 ([43]) but looked for revised June 2000/2001 only in the NEXT year's September issues (which print calendar-year columns) and never opened the Dec 2000 or Dec 2001 issues; it then used the preliminary values for all three 'for consistency'.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Mapped all printings and took the revised June column of each year's December issue.
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: [66]: 'For June 2000, 2001_09 table has calendar year 2000 (Dec) not June ... Could use 2000_09 only' and 'The question likely expects using each issue's June preliminary values'. Its guess about which issue could reprint June was wrong and it never checked the same-year December issue.
first_divergence.consequence: Sum about 1.5% low. Combined with the rate-direction choice below, the final value is about 1% low (within_1pct).

secondary_errors.note: Rate direction and rounding: rounded the USD-per-pound rate to hundredths and divided, instead of rounding GBP-per-USD and multiplying. Because rounding happens before conversion, the two routes differ (this route is ~0.5% higher than Opus's).

remedies.why: It would have flagged 'Sept. p' vs requested 'June'.

remedies.intervention: Rate-direction/rounding convention: 'X to Y rate = Y per 1 X; if the question says to round the rate, round it in that direction before converting'; scope C021 so it does not generalise to date-pinned rates.
remedies.why: The prompt arm reached the right route from an analogous text lesson; this arm raised the right reading at [62] and dropped it.

text_vs_mechanism: Mixed. Vintage and rate direction are convention problems, and text worked for them: the prompt arm, with a latest-printing rule and a USD/INR analogy, matched Opus on both, while the none arm, without that text, got both wrong. Cell selection needs a mechanism: the prompt arm had 'match columns by header, never by position' as text and still slipped a column, and the cards arm slipped a column too. A header-addressed reader or a cited-cell check is required.
notes: Opus itself was low-confidence here (solution.json confidence 'low'; reviewer verdict 'Uncertain' over vintage and rate source), so the vintage and rate conventions are somewhat fragile. For harness design, the robust signal is that both adapted arms made the SAME class of error (off-by-one/last-column read in a wide flattened row whose header is far above the data row), even with a mitigating text rule in context. The none arm shows a separate failure: a repetition loop after compaction pressure. The prompt AGENTS.md also contains a conflicting default ('monthly rows take the first printing'); here the arm luckily overrode it. Growing text lessons can conflict with each other.
